observations: Three black-outlined squares sit side by side across the upper half, each containing a red X-cross over a yellow circle, layered with loose scribbled lines on a white ground.
Below the squares, a black triangle and a magenta rectangle frame dense vertical hatching; to the right, four stacked orange ovals descend along blue vertical strokes against a yellow field.
The whole figure sits on an olive-green background; thick black marks frame the outer edges unevenly, and red, yellow, blue, and magenta strokes break through the white interior at multiple angles.
reading: Three framed squares, each holding a crossed circle, form a row—one more than a face typically carries, giving the structure an unsettled, mechanical feeling. The triangle below sits in nose position by placement alone, while the stacked orange ovals carry the weight of a mouth zone. Olive green holds everything at a distance, even as the interior fills with competing color.
contextAngle: Within the owned nifty-faces subset, this work sits between title neighbors #91 and #93. Where #91 fills a magenta field with a fluid, rounded form, #92 locks its marks inside hard rectangular compartments—a shift from organic sprawl to gridded containment. The collector links nnxyz's line patterns to scrimshaw's engraved repetition.

connections.reason: Title neighbor #93 shares the X-inside-circle motif and a lower zone of dense vertical stripes, making the repeated mark a direct point of comparison across both works.
nnotb #198 shares the same olive-green background and places spiral marks where #92 places crossed circles, contrasting rotational with rectilinear approaches to the same face zone.

lookingQuestion: The three framed squares each contain a similar X-and-circle mark—what differences, if any, can you find between the three versions of that mark?
ambiguities: Title-derived and recorded-creation order align here, but neither confirms making sequence within the broader catalogue.
The orange ovals and blue verticals in the lower right could be read as a mouth-and-chin zone or as a separate structural element; no external evidence resolves this.
